key_concepts: The nose is the main breathing passage and filters air with hairs and mucus.
Nostrils are the two openings of the nose.
The pharynx is a shared passageway for air and food.
The trachea, or windpipe, carries air to and from the lungs.
The trachea is lined with cilia and mucus that trap germs and dust.
The trachea branches into bronchi, which branch into bronchioles.
Bronchioles end in tiny air sacs called alveoli.
The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system and have a spongy texture.
Gas exchange occurs in the alveoli: oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves.
Smoke inhalation can cause suffocation by blocking oxygen from reaching the lungs.
